stage_a.note: Both founders maintain bright smiles and a highly upbeat tone throughout the entire presentation.
They use energetic gestures, enthusiastic vocal inflection, and dynamic pacing to convey strong excitement.
They engage the panel with friendly eye contact and an approachable, welcoming demeanor.

venture.description: A frozen face mask kit combining cryotherapy and superfood ingredients that users mix and freeze at home.
venture.note: The product is called Beauty Pops.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founders introduce themselves, state their ask, and demonstrate how to mix and freeze their cryotherapy face mask.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Rohan asks what happens if he eats the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Paul and Linda confirm that the product is edible.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark jokes that now they are talking his kind of deal.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori reads the natural ingredients aloud.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Rohan takes a bite of the frozen pop and reconsiders eating it.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin questions if the benefit is just the cold and asks if he could get the same result with frozen water.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Linda explains that icing depuffs the skin and leaves behind a nourishing face mask.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Paul adds that they are the first to combine popular ice rollers and face masks into one product.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Rohan asks how they came up with the idea.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Paul explains he is a pharmacist and used his expertise to formulate a scalable version of Linda's DIY frozen banana remedy.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Barbara compliments Linda on having beautiful skin.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Linda shares her background struggling with acne as a teenager and using kitchen ingredients because she couldn't afford skincare.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Barbara asks if Linda made a profession of skincare after her home remedies.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Linda says she started her entrepreneurial journey at 21 with a clothing boutique, where she met Paul.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Paul explains the company name comes from penguins giving pebbles to their mates, saying the company is his pebble to her.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Barbara reacts warmly to the romantic story.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin suggests they transition to discussing the financials.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin notes the valuation and asks what their sales are like.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Paul states their lifetime sales are $890,000.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks how many years it took to achieve those sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Paul replies they launched in March and sold over $100,000 in four days in May.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark asks what triggered the sudden surge in sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Paul explains that they went viral on TikTok.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Linda details posting a video of her mom's before-and-after results, which garnered over 4 million views.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Rohan asks for the cost to make the product and the retail price.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Linda states the landed cost is $9.20 and they sell it for $46.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks how they have financed the company up to this point.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Paul says they self-funded by selling their house and putting everything into the business.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark asks for verification that they actually sold their house.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Linda confirms that they did.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Barbara asks how much money they got from selling the house.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Paul answers that it was $100,000.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin notes viral success fades and asks if they have spent money on digital marketing yet.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Paul confirms that they do utilize paid marketing.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks what their customer acquisition costs are.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Paul states their blended acquisition cost is $7.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks for the margin on the lowest priced kit.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Paul replies that the margin is 80%.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Barbara asks what they are looking for in a shark.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Linda explains they want a shark to help them navigate entering the retail space.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark advises them to focus on their social media success rather than retail, and exits because the product isn't for him.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin says the product simply isn't for him and exits.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Rohan praises their execution but exits due to his lack of expertise in the skincare space.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Linda unpromptedly adds that they are working on a patent to keep the remaining sharks interested.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks what exactly is patent pending about freezing fruit into a pop.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Paul clarifies it is freezing and melting into a mask, and expresses desire to have her on board.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori expresses affection for the founders but advises them to grow slowly, exiting because it's not the right product for her.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Barbara voices concern that their viral success might be a one-hit wonder and expresses mistrust of the retail space.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Paul responds that her concerns highlight the exact kind of guidance they need from an investor.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Barbara thinks aloud about her decision.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin interrupts to joke that his beauty pop is melting.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Barbara concludes that while they have a wonderful business, it is not one for an investor, and exits.

decisions.note: Warns against retail, notes social media is working for them, feels the product isn't a fit for him.
The product is simply not for him.
Praises execution but lacks expertise in the skincare space.
Advises them to grow slowly, states it is not the right product for her.
Concerns about viral success being a one-hit wonder, mistrusts retail space, doesn't think it's a business for an investor.

record.notes: A model is present on stage to demonstrate the product but does not speak.
